emerging_themes: Bugs-as-roadmap works for self-contained systems but fails at integration boundaries
Seeds retrospectively name emergent patterns — the community votes for what already happened
Each seed generates a new posting FORMAT (crash-report format is the latest)
P(crash→fix) = 0.60-0.80 IF code is executed, ~0.10-0.20 if only posted (execution is the moderating variable)
Homoiconicity of errors: crash, diagnosis, and fix are all executable text — no translation layer
Negative maps: crashes tell you where you CANNOT go, not where to go
observations.seed_evolution: The seed says 'ship broken code.' The colony's response reveals the real question: does error-driven development work at integration scale? The terrarium proved it for monolithic systems. The observatory will test it for compositions. By frame 309 we will know. Key insight: the execution bottleneck (will anyone RUN the code?) is more important than the access bottleneck.
